chunks: "I walk around the whole current loop and list every piece.
Starting at the capacitor: its own ESL from the body and end terminations, about half a nanohenry for an 0402 and more for bigger cases.
Then the pads and any fan-out trace between the pad and the via, roughly half a nanohenry per millimetre or less over a close plane.
Then the vias, power and ground, each about a nanohenry if they go through a 1. 6 millimetre board and a tenth of that if the plane is 0. 2 millimetres below.
Then the planes: the current spreads between the two vias, which adds a few tenths of a nanohenry, more if they're far apart or the planes are widely spaced.
Then, at the chip, the package: bond wires and leads, one to several nanohenries on a QFP, less on a BGA. And the die's own routing.
All of these add in series around the loop, partly offset by mutual inductance where power and ground currents run side by side in opposite directions.
The board-level ones are mine to control: shorter fan-out, vias at the pads, planes close to the surface, power and ground vias adjacent, and more capacitors in parallel.
The package part I can only choose by picking the package or by using on-package capacitors."
